stem:
Damini wants an easier way to compute $97 \times 103$ while keeping the same value.

Which claim correctly chooses and justifies a decomposition?

options.text: Call the answer the phrase place-value base alone, and stop.
Rewrite as $(100-3)(100+5)$, even though that product is not equal to $97 \times 103$.
Use $97 \times 100$ alone, because $100$ is the standout round number near $103$.

teacher.key_rationale: 97=100-3 and 103=100+3, so the difference-of-squares identity keeps the value. Naming place-value base alone, using an unequal rewrite, or grabbing the round 100 all miss the equal-decomposition hinge.
